title: Fix FP8 KV cache alignment edge case impacting decode correctness + perf
author: Grace Kim
body:
Context: During the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint we saw a bimodal behavior on FP8 decode for a subset of shapes (most visible on H100, but reproducible on A100). In some runs decode throughput dropped ~8–15% vs baseline, and in worse cases we observed occasional correctness mismatches (rare, but repeatable) when running with certain max_seq_len + page size combinations. This was correlated with a KV cache layout where the K/V page base pointer could be misaligned relative to the vectorized load/store assumptions in the FP8 decode path.

Root cause: The FP8 KV cache decode kernel assumes the K/V page base is aligned to 16 bytes (and that the per-head stride preserves this alignment). When the cache is allocated with a base alignment of 16 but the page offset is computed in bytes and then cast to the vector type, some page offsets produce a misaligned pointer (e.g. when page_size * element_size does not preserve 16B alignment after accounting for per-layer/per-head packing). On H100 this mostly manifested as degraded performance due to unaligned memory transactions; on a narrower set of cases we also hit an incorrect vectorized path in the dequant/load sequence (we were effectively reading across a boundary when the pointer wasn’t aligned as expected).

Fix: (1) Make the alignment contract explicit at the KV cache allocator and layout layer: ensure page base pointers and per-page offsets are aligned to 16B for FP8 mode (and 8B for the fallback scalar path). (2) Add a guarded fallback in the FP8 decode kernel: if alignment is not satisfied at runtime, route to the scalar/packed load path (still correct; slightly slower) rather than executing the vectorized path. (3) Add coverage: a unit test that constructs KV caches with page sizes / seq lengths that previously produced misalignment and verifies decode outputs against the baseline FP16 path (tolerances consistent with existing FP8 decode tests).

Perf impact: On the cases that regressed, this restores the expected decode throughput (we saw +7–12% tokens/s vs the broken FP8 path; net +4–9% vs baseline, depending on scheduler mix). No measurable impact on the common aligned cases.

Notes: This change is intentionally conservative. We keep the vectorized path fast when alignment holds, and we never silently execute it when alignment doesn’t. This should reduce benchmark variance from cache-shape quirks and avoid canary correctness incidents. Follow-up work (separate PR) will tighten shape constraints in the kernel registry so we avoid selecting FP8 decode kernels for unsupported alignment regimes.

Testing: - Added unit tests under runtime/tests/gpu for KV cache alignment edge cases. - Ran the benchmark harness on H100 (sm90) and A100 (sm80) for a representative decode-heavy workload (short prefill, long decode). - Ran correctness sanity suite (golden prompts) locally for FP8 mode.

Rollout: No flag changes. This is a bugfix under the existing FP8 decode flag. Safe to ship; canary should show reduced variance and elimination of the observed mismatch case.

Checklist: [x] Repro case captured and attached (see logs in artifacts link) [x] Fix includes correctness guardrails [x] Unit test added [x] Bench rerun on H100/A100 [x] SRE notified for canary expectations (reduced variance)

Artifacts: - Benchmark run IDs: benchlab://runs/2026-02-16/fp8-kv-align-hotfix (H100), benchlab://runs/2026-02-16/fp8-kv-align-hotfix-a100 (A100) - Nsight snippet: benchlab://profiles/2026-02-16/fp8-kv-align-case3 (shows reduced unaligned transactions after fix)
commits: runtime/kv_cache: document + enforce 16B alignment contract for FP8 pages
runtime/kernels/fp8_decode: add alignment check + scalar fallback path
tests: add KV cache alignment edge-case correctness test
bench: add debug counters for alignment/fallback rate (behind BENCH_DEBUG)
review_conversation:
Yuki Sato: Can we guarantee allocator alignment across all KV layouts, or are we relying on page_size being friendly? I’m worried we’ll still hit misalignment if a future layout changes.
Grace Kim (author): Good call. This PR enforces alignment in two places: allocator ensures page base alignment; layout rounds per-page stride to preserve 16B alignment in FP8 mode. I also left the runtime kernel guard so if we ever regress the contract we still stay correct.

Isabella Rossi: Please add a metric/debug counter so we can see if we’re unexpectedly hitting the scalar fallback in benchmarks.
Grace Kim: Added BENCH_DEBUG counter + metadata field in artifact export. It’s off in production.

Noah Patel: The correctness issue is scary — do we know if it’s actual wrong bytes or numeric drift? Also, please confirm this doesn’t change default kernel selection.
Grace Kim: It’s wrong bytes in the vectorized load path under misalignment (confirmed by reading back K/V and comparing). Kernel selection is unchanged; we just avoid executing the unsafe path.

Julian Moore: Scheduler might change effective alignment rate due to different page reuse patterns. Do we need to gate by scheduler config?
Grace Kim: Not needed; alignment is a property of layout + offsets. Scheduler affects reuse, but shouldn’t affect alignment itself. The fallback counter should help validate we’re not hitting unexpected paths.

Approvals: Yuki Sato (approved), Isabella Rossi (approved), Noah Patel (approved).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Connor O'Brien. Squash commit message: "Fix FP8 KV cache alignment edge case impacting decode correctness + perf (#19871)"
release_notes: Runtime: FP8 decode KV cache alignment bugfix. Prevents rare correctness mismatches and restores expected decode throughput for affected shapes by enforcing alignment and adding a safe fallback path.
